behaviour.transferFee: none in the current implementation; an upgrade could add one
behaviour.blocklist: `transfer` and `transferFrom` revert when the CALLER is blocked, `transferFrom` also when `from` is blocked: a blocked vault can neither pull a deposit nor pay; a blocked address still RECEIVES; its balance can then be destroyed
behaviour.upgrade: the proxy admin's owner can replace the implementation
recipientRefusals: the token contract itself (a transfer to it reverts)

verified.source: https://docs.usdt0.to/technical-documentation/deployments (the USDT0 publisher's list; fetched by agent 409 on 2026-11-18, sha256 baa823860bbd3648...)

loopback fork of Arbitrum One at block 525506294 (public fork source arb1.arbitrum.io, read-only): proxy slots, implementation code keccak, owner and proxy admin owner (one Safe, 3 of 5), blocklist behaviour with the vault in each role

fee.collection: accrued in the vault outside the backing; anyone calls sweepFees() and the vault pays the recipient
fee.networkFee: the depositor pays the deposit transaction; the relayer pays the release transaction, up to 0.5 gwei: while the network's gas price is above that the release waits

finality.rule: A deposit is attested when its block is at or below the block the signer's own Arbitrum One node reports as finalized (its batch is in a finalized Ethereum block).
finality.reorg: Signers read only finalized blocks; a deposit that leaves the canonical chain before finality is never attested. Every mint waits 12 hours on the L2; the relayer does not execute a mint whose deposit is not in the vault's finalized deposit chain and the guardians cancel it. A credited mint with no deposit holds later releases instead of paying them.

deposit.recipientEncoding: bytes32: the 20-byte L2 address left-padded with zeros
steps: approve the vault for the amount on the USD₮0 contract
call deposit(amount, l2Recipient) on the vault
after source finality and the 12 hour mint delay the L2 token credits amount less 0.05% to l2Recipient
refusals: an amount below minDeposit or above maxDeposit, or one that would pass the cap
an l2Recipient that is zero or longer than 20 bytes
do not name a contract as l2Recipient unless it can move the token

a deposit while the asset contract is not in the pinned state (issuer fee, pause, replaced or upgraded token, vault blocked): the vault or the token refuses it, and the signers attest nothing for the route until the state is back

notes: a recipient the issuer has blocked is still PAID by this token (only the sender side is checked); the issuer can then destroy that balance. The burn names the recipient and cannot be redirected
never name the token contract itself (a transfer to it reverts) as the recipient: the release of such a burn can never be paid and the burned amount stays locked
the relayer pays at most 0.5 gwei per gas: while the network's gas price is above that ceiling a release waits (it is not lost) and is paid when the price falls
the smallest exit is l2MinBurn (20); the fee of an exit covers the relayer's gas only up to a gas price that grows with the amount (docs/BRIDGE-EVM-NETWORKS.md section 9.1)
